title: Say what a source can't show
statement: A lesson says plainly what its source cannot show, and models declining an inference the source does not support.
detail: A reading course's lesson-writing playbook makes this its distinctive register: the lesson says plainly what a source or representation cannot show, without hedging into vagueness and without overclaiming, and models honest refusal of unsupported inferences (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/LESSON-AUTHORING-PLAYBOOK.md`). A course proposal's transfer layer allows teaching students to explain why an option is unsupported (`grade3-reading/artifacts/knowledge-first-reading-course-proposal-2026-07-09/03-transfer-practice-layer.md`).

evidence.quote: vagueness and without overclaiming. Model honest refusal of unsupported inferences.
